In mid-November, following a nationwide halt to U.S. flight departures, social media users shared claims about connections between Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy; his son-in-law, U.S. Rep.-elect Michael Alfonso, a Wisconsin Republican; and Air Space Intelligence — the company behind a new artificial intelligence-powered system used by the Federal Aviation Administration.
On Nov. 13, the FAA ordered a nationwide ground stop after communications problems affected air traffic control facilities. The incident happened three days after the agency announced the nationwide expansion of an AI-supported traffic management system called SMART, developed by ASI.
Some posts claimed Alfonso had financial ties to ASI or received the FAA contract through Duffy, while others linked the company to the shutdown. For instance, one Facebook post (archived) read:
On Friday, the FAA grounded every plane in America.
The AI air traffic system at the center of it belongs to Air Space Intelligence. In June, Sean Duffy's department gave them an $875 million contract.
Before that, the company's PAC donated to Duffy's son-in-law, 26-year-old Michael Alfonso. He just won Duffy's old seat in Congress.
Americans deserve answers.
Another post (archived) on X stated, "Sean Duffy's son in law owns the AI company responsible for this FAA disaster yall."
Versions of the claim circulated on multiple social media platforms, including Reddit, X, Instagram and Facebook. Snopes readers also asked whether Alfonso or Duffy owned ASI, whether Alfonso received a multimillion-dollar FAA contract and whether campaign donations influenced the deal.
In short, Air Space Intelligence's PAC did contribute to Alfonso's campaign in March, and the company later received an FAA contract worth up to $875.95 million. However, we found no evidence that Alfonso owned ASI or that the donation influenced the contract award. The FAA also denied that the company's SMART system caused the Nov. 13 shutdown, and rather pointed to problems with its older communications network.
Alfonso's team said he had no part in awarding the FAA contract and that the campaign donation broke no laws or ethics rules, adding, "Nobody trades an $875 million federal contract for a $2,500 check." The FAA said in a statement that "each FAA contract goes through a rigorous, competitive process guided by nonpartisan career experts and personnel." We have also reached out to Air Space Intelligence and will update this report if we receive a response.
Here's what we know about the rumor:
ASI's PAC donated to Alfonso's campaign
According to a filing with the Federal Election Commission, Air Space Intelligence's political action committee donated $2,500 to Alfonso's congressional campaign on March 31:
(Federal Election Commission)
Alfonso's campaign also reported the same contribution:
(Federal Election Commission)
Some social media posts and articles, however, mentioned a larger sum of $12,500. That likely stemmed from a Raw Story article, which cited that amount, but later issued a correction.
News outlets reported on Alfonso's campaign donations even before the FAA shutdown. For instance, in March, ProPublica reported that his campaign received money from lobbyists and companies with interests before the Department of Transportation.
Did Alfonso or Duffy have financial ties to ASI?
Some social media posts claimed Alfonso owned Air Space Intelligence. Snopes readers also asked whether he invested in the company or benefited financially from its FAA contract.
However, we found no evidence supporting these claims. Neither Alfonso nor Duffy was listed among ASI's founders or executives. Alfonso's financial disclosure from April also didn't list any investment in ASI, although it only covered the period until October 2025. Similarly, Duffy's 2026 financial disclosure didn't list ASI among his investments.
In a statement to Snopes, Alfonso said, "Family ties don't earn anyone special treatment, and my father-in-law knows better than anyone that I think for myself." His team did not directly answer whether he ever owned shares or had any other financial interest in ASI.
Who received the $875M FAA contract?
Some social media posts claimed that Duffy awarded a multimillion-dollar FAA contract directly to his son-in-law, sometimes describing it as a no-bid contract. For example, one Bluesky user wrote, "In a surprise to no one, Sean Duffy gave a No Bid contract to his son-in-law to install the AI program into the FAA's system."
However, the USAspending.gov database showed the contract was awarded to Air Space Intelligence, not Alfonso:
(www.usaspending.gov)
The contract began on June 23 and could run for 12 years. Its maximum potential value is $875.95 million, but this does not mean ASI has already received all of that amount.
"No laws or House Ethics rules were violated," Alfonso's team told us via email, adding that "By law, PACs can give up to $5,000 per election. Nobody trades an $875 million federal contract for a $2,500 check."
According to federal records, the FAA received 12 offers before awarding the contract to ASI. The records classified the award as competitive, although they did not identify the other bidders or explain how ASI was selected. Bloomberg reported "the startup beat out larger competitors Palantir Technologies Inc. and Thales SA."
The FAA said in a statement that: "each FAA contract goes through a rigorous, competitive process guided by nonpartisan career experts and personnel. The FAA awarded the contract to Air Space Intelligence (ASI) following an innovative challenge with three vendors who demonstrated the highest levels of reliability, operational performance, and efficiency." The agency did not say whether Duffy was personally involved in the decision, or whether there was any potential conflict of interest involving him or Alfonso.
The FAA announced its search for a company to develop the system in September 2025, months before ASI's PAC donated to Alfonso's campaign, and announced ASI as the winner in June. We found no public evidence that the donation influenced the contract award.
Alfonso's team said he had no part in awarding the FAA contract, pointing out that he was a congressional candidate at the time, and not a government official. In a statement to Snopes, Alfonso also said, "I can't be bought," adding that he would consider each bill separately, including any future FAA funding requests, and "vote based on what's best for Wisconsin."
What caused the Nov. 13 FAA shutdown?
The FAA said its new AI system, SMART, did not cause the nationwide flight shutdown on Nov. 13. During a news briefing the next day, Duffy explained it "is a system that's not tied into or connected to the systems that went down yesterday. It's a tool that gives a prompt to one of our flight managers that they can accept or deny, but it's just better information flowing to them," summarizing that "SMART had zero impact on the occurrences yesterday."
Similarly, ASI wrote on X on Nov. 13 that the "current ground stop is not based on or a result of the SMART system, any product of ASI or our integration with FAA and ATC."
According to a Nov. 15 statement, the issue involved the FAA's older communications network. The agency identified two possible locations connected to the problem: a site in Arkansas, where contractor L3Harris was installing a new router, and another in Texas. L3Harris confirmed in a news release it was cooperating with the FAA's investigation. As of this writing, the exact cause of the shutdown was still under investigation.

The headlines may be dominated by artificial intelligence and electoral politics, but beneath it all, another debate constantly simmers, forever threatening to erupt.
Men weren’t always “bad at friendship”
History has a solution for the male loneliness crisis.
I write, of course, of the great male friendship debate.
On one side: writers, journalists, and academics who fret over rising male loneliness, the emotional impact of friendless men on their partners, and the threat to society posed by atomized and isolated fellas. On the other: those who defend male friendships built around shared activities rather than heart-to-hearts.
These arguments often talk past each other. But the historian Tiffany Watt Smith offered me a way to think differently about both: that the gender roles undergirding the conversation are not nearly as fixed as they seem.
“I can definitely tell you that men in the past had much more intimate and romantic and involved friendships than we see today, for sure,” said Smith, who has published a number of books on the histories of friendship and emotions. “The idea that women are the kind of great experts in friendship is a really modern idea.”
I talked with Smith about Aristotle’s idea of the “perfect” friendship (it has to be between two dudes), how gendered notions of friendship inverted in the 19th century, and what men seeking deeper emotional connection from their buddies can learn from the past. You can hear that conversation and and more on the latest episode of Explain It to Me, Vox’s weekly call-in podcast.
Below is an excerpt of my conversation with Smith, edited for length and clarity. You can listen to the full episode on Apple Podcasts, Spotify, or wherever you get your podcasts. If you’d like to submit a question, send an email to askvox@vox.com or call 1-800-618-8545.
How do male friendships today compare to those of the past?
For thousands of years, it was really men who were considered the great experts in knowing how to form the highest kinds of friendships and the most intimate kind of bonds. And their friendships were considered the most meaningful and enduring and deep kind of friendships.
If you look back at David and Jonathan in the Bible or Achilles and Patroclus in the Iliad, you see these very dynamic, committed male friendships. When we look at the writings of Aristotle in the fourth-century BC, he’s talking about the deepest kind of friendship. He calls it the perfect friendship.
And this is between two men who he sees as soulmates. And he does say that there are other kinds of friendship, which are lesser friendships. He says you might make friends because it’s kind of convenient or because you enjoy doing the same kinds of things, or maybe you’re trying to help each other out. There’s a kind of quid pro quo-type of friendship. So he does see these kinds of friendship all around him. And he says women do those kinds of friendships.
One of the most famous pieces of writing about friendship ever is Michel de Montaigne’s essay “On Friendship.” Montaigne was a 16th-century essayist and lawyer, and he had this very, very close and committed friendship with another writer called La Boétie. And then after La Boétie died very unexpectedly, Montaigne wrote about their friendship and he said they had this kind of ideal friendship, the kind that Aristotle wrote about, this meeting of souls, and that this was rare and extraordinary.
And he was very explicit. He said, “Men can have these kinds of friendships.” But he very explicitly said, “Women are just incapable of having this kind of perfect friendship. They don’t have the kind of emotional stamina. They’re not clever enough. They’re not educated enough. Their souls aren’t strong enough, essentially, to withstand the complexities and difficulties of friendship.” So it’s a complete inversion from what we see today.
You used this word when you started: romantic. What did you mean by that? Was the Aristotelian conception of a perfect male friendship, was there a kind of romantic element in the way that we use the word romance?
Historians call this style of friendship “romantic friendship.” It doesn’t necessarily mean that they were having a physically active relationship or that they were having sex. They did see themselves as a partnership, and some of these male friends talked about themselves as married. This was a marriage of soul.
“Friendship is something that we have to negotiate on an individual basis. Each friendship is completely singular and we have to work out its rules.”
There’s a very important tombstone in Christ’s College in Cambridge, which commemorates these two doctors in the 16th century who basically lived their whole lives together. They traveled together, they did their research together and so on. And when they died, they were buried together. And the tomb does look like a conventional tomb between a husband and wife.
Now, we don’t know anything about their relationship in practice. I mean, the thing that really matters is the fact that this friendship, because it was commemorated as a friendship, the fact that it could be commemorated so vividly and publicly in such an extravagant way shows us that this is a culture that accepts and idealizes this kind of male friendship.
So how do we get from there to here?
Beginning in the 18th century and certainly by the 19th century, there’s a series of things that happen. One is that we get a distinction between the public space of the workplaces, cities are expanding, offices start to exist. The male sphere is fashioned as one of being in public, being a more rational sphere, and the female sphere starts to be connected with the home and intimacy and emotion.
Those ideas have been kind of floating around for a while, but they start to get really consolidated in the 19th century. And at the same time, a new ideal of femininity starts to emerge and it becomes a real sort of middle-class aspirational goal for women that they have very close friendships, almost as evidence that they can do all of these things.
Young girls in this era are taught a very particular style of friendship, which is, again, it’s very romantic. There’s lots of kissing and declarations of love and so on, but also it’s shown to be very committed. It’s very thoughtful, it’s very caring. And this is seen to be a kind of training ground for motherhood and for marriage.
At the end of the 19th century, we start to portray male friendships as kind of blundering and superficial and lacking in intimacy. And then of course, men carry on having close friendships, but by the beginning of the 20th century, another nail in the coffin, as it were, happens, which is that there’s a rise in understanding of homosexuality across Europe and America, and gay culture becomes much more visible.
In that moment, men become really anxious about having intimate and close relationships with other men. They’re worried about what that looks like and how that might be read. And that, in addition, leads to these anxieties about close male friendships.
If some guy is hearing this and is interested in having more fulfilling friendships, but he doesn’t know how to get there, where might he start?
The thing about history is that it shows us how much things have changed, but it also reminds us that things keep changing and can change again.
We’ve had this amazing history of these very romantic, intense, effusive male friendships. I think a lot of men probably would find that kind of overwhelming and unappealing as a model of friendship, but is there something in between? And one of the things I think that is important to remember is that we can make these changes and these shifts in style and these shifts in the patterns and our approaches to friendships.
One thing that I think it’s really worth listeners remembering is that since friendship has changed in the past, it can change again. There’s nothing biologically innate about the inability to make friends.
Which is freeing, the fact that friendship is not a fixed category for men or for women and that things can be what you want them to be. You’re not held back by some innate aspect of our biology.
I think that’s absolutely true. We get this notion that, well, men are sort of naturally worse at making friends or something, or they naturally have less kind of desire to connect with other people. That’s completely not true. The history of male friendships shows us that that is completely not true. So we can be released from that idea.
There isn’t an obvious, perfect, one-size-fits-all version of friendship. Friendship is something that we have to negotiate on an individual basis. Each friendship is completely singular and we have to work out its rules. What is my style of friendship? What is your style of friendship? How can we find something in the between so that we understand how to communicate and how not to hurt each other and how to build trust between each other?

The Karnataka government has reportedly halted the registration of new taxis operated by Vingroup-backed Green SM days after clearing its operation within the state. Alongside this, the transport department is said to be planning to make fare meters compulsory for all cabs, including those operating through ride-hailing platforms such as Ola and Uber. Transport Minister Byrathi Suresh cited the need to protect the interests of local taxi owners and drivers as an explanation for the ban, as per a report by Moneycontrol. The state government has directed transport department officials to stop registering new Green SM taxis until further orders, even as around 100 vehicles operated by the company have already been registered to ply on Karnataka roads. That said, the state government is yet to take a final call on whether Green SM will be allowed to continue its operations in Karnataka. Questions sent to Green SM remained unanswered at the time of publication. The story will be updated upon receiving a response. The latest action follows protests by Bengaluru-based private transport associations such as Karnataka Rajya Chalakara Parishath and Peace Auto Union. The e-taxi operator, part of Vietnam's Vingroup, which also operates electric car OEM Vinfast, received an aggregator licence from the Karnataka Transport Department in November 2026, valid until September 2031. Protesting associations have questioned the licensing process and alleged that Green SM's vehicles were registered without meeting mandatory requirements, including digital fare meters, taxi display boards, GPS equipment and driver documentation. They have also raised concerns about the impact of another large fleet operator on the earnings of existing taxi drivers, particularly those who have taken loans to purchase their vehicles, seeking an examination of the permissions granted to the company and the potential impact on local operators from the Karnataka Governor. Taxi and auto unions in the state have a long track record of opposing ride-hailing platforms like Uber, Ola and Rapido for their fares, compensation practices and vehicle formats like bike-taxis. Green SM's planned Bengaluru entry is part of a wider India expansion strategy. It is already operational in Delhi NCR and Hyderabad and touched the 15 Lakh rides milestone earlier this month. Green SM started India operations in June this year. It is now preparing to expand across six geographies, and has secured aggregator licences in Delhi, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh and Karnataka, with plans to enter Bengaluru and Chennai. Ride-Hailing Platforms Face Regular Roadblocks Karnataka also plans to introduce mandatory fare meters for all taxis, including those operating through app-based aggregators, the state’s transport minister said. The transport department is preparing the necessary draft rules and legal provisions, with the government warning that vehicles found violating the prescribed fare requirements could be seized. The proposed move follows complaints from taxi owners and drivers seeking a uniform fare structure and alleging that aggregators have been exploiting them. The emphasis on physical meters comes as cab aggregators like Uber, Ola and Rapido face increasing scrutiny over fare structures, additional charges and booking practices. In August, the transport department issued notices to Ola, Uber and Rapido over alleged violations of government-notified fares following complaints from driver associations that the aggregators were charging passengers fares different from those prescribed by the state government and were not paying drivers the stipulated amounts. More recently, the Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) imposed penalties on Rapido and Ola over prompts asking passengers to increase their payments when drivers were not accepting the original fares. The regulator found that messages and prompts suggesting additional payments constituted dark patterns, including confirmed shaming. The CCPA also said it had initiated proceedings against Uber and Namma Yatri over similar practices, with investigations ongoing. However, the proposal remains under judicial scrutiny after the Supreme Court questioned FSSAI's proposed 365-day voluntary compliance period. FSSAI is yet to notify the final regulations, noting that it could take approximately four months to prepare and finalise the draft amendment regulations.

On the intervening night of November 8 and 9, over 250 PM2.5 data points from Delhi were missing on the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) website, according to an analyst at the Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air (CREA).
Scientist and air quality analyst Manoj Kumar tweeted the statistics in the early hours of November 9. According to him, out of the 59 monitoring stations, as seen on the official website of the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB), only 14 stations reported complete data, while the remaining 45 had at least one missing hourly observation.
Missing hourly PM2.5 data raises concerns over Delhi’s air quality assessment.
Since midnight on 8 November until 5 am on 9 November, 227 hourly PM2.5 observations were missing across 59 CPCB monitoring stations in Delhi. Only 14 stations reported complete data, while the remaining 45 had at least one missing hourly observation.
A key concern is that many missing readings occurred when concentrations approached the monitoring instruments’ upper measurement limit of 1,000 µg/m³. These observations should not simply be treated as missing when calculating hourly or daily averages or deriving AQI. Doing so could underestimate pollution levels. For a conservative assessment, such readings should be flagged as potentially exceeding the measurement range, with 1,000 µg/m³ considered as a lower-bound value rather than treating them as zero or excluding them without qualification.
Mundka recorded the highest number of missing hourly observations (10), followed by Dwarka Sector 8, IIT Delhi, Nehru Nagar, Pusa IITM and Uttam Nagar, with eight missing hours each.
There is also an unusual pattern at some stations. IGNOU Maidan Garhi, Cantonment Area, Siri Fort and Tikri Kalan recorded PM2.5 concentrations below 30 µg/m³ (Cleanest) during parts of this episode. Given the pollution levels elsewhere, these readings warrant verification for possible instrument or data-quality issues before being used in final averages or AQI calculations.
Reliable air-quality assessment during pollution episodes requires both complete data and transparent treatment of readings that exceed instrument measurement limits.
— Dr. Manoj Kumar (@manoj_kumar_nr) November 9, 2026
Air Quality Index, or AQI, turns air quality data for eight pollutants into one number and one name, providing an easy-to-understand picture of air quality. According to the All India AQI Dashboard, the pollutants are PM10, PM2.5, NO2, SO2, CO, O3, Pb, and NH3. (Lead is not monitored at every station.)
Delhi’s average AQI on the night of Diwali was as follows, according to the CPCB.
However, between 1 am and 3 am on the Diwali night, over 30 monitoring stations were not showing any PM2.5 data. Over the course of the night, more stations failed.
A day after, as the mystery of missing data caused an outrage, the hourly air quality readings missing from the CPCB website became available on the Delhi Pollution Control Committee (DPCC) website, which showed that the PM2.5 concentration went up to a staggering 3500 micrograms per cubic metre and beyond, which is around 60 times its standard value.
Below is the reading from Mundka station:
Below is the reading from JNU station:
Why does the Missing Data Matter?
India’s air quality figures come from monitoring stations run by state pollution control boards and committees, such as DPCC in Delhi. Stations send their readings to CPCB every 15 minutes. CPCB calculates each station’s AQI by finding a sub-index for every pollutant and taking the highest one. It then publishes the results on its portal, the SAMEER app and its daily bulletin.
A sub-index is the AQI score for a single pollutant on its own. Each pollutant is measured in different units and has a different “safe” range. For example, PM2.5 is in micrograms per cubic metre, and CO is in milligrams per cubic metre. So CPCB converts each pollutant’s reading to the same 0-500 scale, and that converted number is its sub-index.
If the PM2.5 has a sub-index of 75, SO2 has 63, and NO2 has 38, the station’s overall AQI is the highest of these, so here it is 75, driven by PM2.5. One bad pollutant is enough to push the AQI into a worse category, even if the others are fine.
If one looks carefully at the above screenshot from 12 midnight on November 9 from the Anand Vihar monitoring station, one would see that the 24-hour average of the PM2.5 pollutant is the 24-hour average AQI for that particular monitoring station. One would also note that the highest average sub-index determines the AQI.
Now, if PM2.5, which gives a measure of fine particulate matter in the air and is also highest during Diwali due to the bursting of firecrackers, goes missing, the average AQI reading underestimates the pollution in the air to a great extent. According to a Hindustan Times report, if one considers the released readings, Delhi’s AQI for 24 hours until 9 am on November 9 was 384 on a 500 scale against the 370 figure published by CPCB.
Why did the Data Go Missing?
According to Kumar’s post on X (shared when the missing data had not been released), Mundka recorded the highest number of missing hourly observations (10), followed by Dwarka Sector 8, IIT Delhi, Nehru Nagar, Pusa IITM and Uttam Nagar, with eight missing hours each.
Interestingly, the highest reading also came from Mundka at 3,744 µg/m³ at 2 am on November 9. JNU was at 3,023 at 4 am the same night and NSUT’s West Campus at 3,008 at 5 am. Eleven of DPCC’s stations went past 2,000 micrograms per cubic metre.
The CPCB released an official statement on November 10 addressing the data gaps, saying that particulate analysers like PM2.5 were calibrated for 0-1,000 µg/m³. Under the automated validation, hourly readings beyond that range are treated as “outside range” and left out of the computation. CPCB conceded this “may appear as a data gap” during extreme episodes like Diwali firecracker bursting. Those hours don’t count towards the 24-hour average for that station. It also stated that the methodology for processing data beyond the system’s design range is “under review”, with internal deliberations underway.
On November 11, Kumar posted on X, if the 255 missing PM2.5 data points were replaced with 1,000 µg/m³, the upper measurement limit cited by CPCB, the average showed a 49% increase, from 269 to 400 µg/m³.
Alt News spoke to Kumar, who also told us that while the DPCC continued to record data above 1000 micrograms per cubic metre, it was the CPCB, the body ultimately entrusted with calculating and releasing AQI findings, that did not register it. “DPCC had measured and displayed PM 2.5 concentration above 1000 on that day. But it was not reflected on the CPCB website.”
Explaining the process and the gaps, Kumar said, “Let’s say that the instrument’s operating range is between 0 and 1000. But if it is going above 1000, there will be some uncertainty, but uncertainty can be estimated.”
Even in his November 9 post, Kumar made the point that the readings had gone missing as the concentration readings approached 1000. “These observations should not simply be treated as missing when calculating hourly or daily averages or deriving AQI. Doing so could underestimate pollution levels. For a conservative assessment, such readings should be flagged as potentially exceeding the measurement range, with 1,000 µg/m³ considered as a lower-bound value rather than treating them as zero or excluding them without qualification,” he wrote.
Furthermore, to calculate AQI, one would need to have at least 16 hours in a day, if not all 24 hours of data. So missing out on important data points during peak pollution periods underrepresents the AQI value.
It’s also worth noting that aur quality monitoring is not cheap: A 2018 Hindustan Times report put the cost of a conventional station at up to Rs 5 crore.

In mid-November, an alleged Truth Social post by U.S. President Donald Trump claiming that disruptions to food and banking services were imminent spread on social media.
A screenshot of the alleged post circulated on TikTok, Threads, and Facebook several days before customers at a handful of major U.S. banks experienced service outages on Nov. 16. JPMorgan Chase confirmed that a technical issue was behind the disruptions, according to the Associated Press.
The purported screenshot read:
URGENT: New intelligence and global developments indicate there could be serious disruptions to our food supply, banking system, and critical services in the coming weeks. To protect your family, I strongly recommend that Americans take the following steps immediately:
- Stock up on at least 90 DAYS of food, water, and essential supplies.
- Withdraw your cash from the bank and keep it on hand.
- Be prepared for potential internet and cell service outages.
This is about being prepared, not panicking. The risks are real, and it's better to be ready now than to be caught off guard later.
I want to thank Diane Cavoto, who has been sounding the alarm on this for months. She has been right, and her guidance has helped many Americans get prepared.
Thank you for your attention to this matter. President DONALD J TRUMP.
(Accessed via X)
We found no evidence of Trump sharing the above post on any of his social media accounts. As such, we've rated the screenshot fake.
Searches for variations of the quote on Google, DuckDuckGo (archived) and Bing uncovered no reporting from reliable media outlets connecting it to the president, which would have been the case if it were authentic. We searched for various phrases within the purported post, including "New intelligence and global developments," "Stock up on at least 90 DAYS of food" and "This is about being prepared, not panicking," none of which returned any relevant results.
Likewise, searches of Roll Call's archive of Trump's posts on X and Truth Social and Trump's Truth, a website dedicated to archiving his Truth Social posts, did not return any results for posts resembling the screenshot.
As of this writing, we were unable to determine who originally shared the fake post.
For further reading, Snopes has frequently debunked many fake quotes attributed to Trump.

A molecular signal in the blood helps identify microscopic changes that precede the development of ovarian cancer, researchers have found, in a potential diagnostic breakthrough for a disease often discovered after it has already spread.
For decades, efforts to detect ovarian cancer earlier have focused on finding smaller tumours, the researchers noted in their report published on Tuesday in Nature Medicine.
“We asked a fundamentally different question: What if we could identify the earliest molecular warning signs before invasive cancer even develops?” study leader Rajan Gogna of the Hoag Family Cancer Institute in Newport Beach, California, said in a statement. Ovarian cancer often begins with microscopic changes in the lining of the fallopian tubes.
The precancerous lesions are known as serous tubal intraepithelial carcinoma (STIC). The new study found that women with this precursor condition have elevated blood levels of an RNA molecule called Tu-Stroma.
When researchers measured Tu-Stroma in blood, they detected STIC in 92.3% of affected women and correctly identified 98.2% of healthy women. In women with genetic risk factors for ovarian cancer, approximately 72% of positive results would be accurate, while negative results would be correct nearly 100% of the time, they reported. “For women at high risk, this could transform how we approach prevention,” co-author Esha Madan, also of Hoag, said in a statement.
Many such women face difficult decisions about preventive surgery to remove their fallopian tubes and ovaries. “Today, decisions about preventive surgery are largely guided by inherited risk, without knowing whether precancerous lesions are actually present,” Madan said. “Our discovery could eventually provide that missing biological information.”

Dust off that Hitachi and put your Slack on “Do not disturb,” because AO3 is back online, baby.
After weeks off the internet due to an unspecified security incident, the Organization for Transformative Works (OTW), the nonprofit that runs the hugely popular fan fiction forum, announced on November 15 that service had been restored.
“We understand that the wait and uncertainty surrounding AO3’s return have been difficult, and we apologize for the inconvenience,” the statement reads. “We greatly appreciate your support during the downtime, and continued patience as our volunteers work hard to return AO3 to its full functionality.”
The news came as a pleasant surprise to AO3’s devoted fans, as the website had announced in late October that restoring service could take between two to four weeks. To that end, the OTW statement says that some of the site’s features, such as user icons and external work importing, have been temporarily disabled in order to expedite the site’s return. It also warned that users “may experience a delay before AO3 loads,” due to “high traffic.”
Founded in 2007, AO3 is one of the most popular fan fiction forums on the internet, boasting more than 11 million users and over 18 million original works. Following its temporary shutdown, many devastated fans started sharing Google Docs of their favorite fanfics, sparking some concerns among authors worried about AI scraping and their work being posted to other websites without their permission. Others resorted to other platforms to get their Dramione or Hollanov fix, such as Tumblr, which reported a 75 percent jump in new sign-ups among users between the ages of 18 and 25, according to data shared with WIRED.
Throughout the 17-day shutdown, AO3 has remained vague about the causes of the security breach. In its statement announcing its return, OTW said that while it has “no reason to believe that the user database was compromised,” it can’t rule out the possibility; the website recommends users change their passwords “as a precaution.” The site is also pairing with a security firm “to help prevent future incidents.”
Though the suggestion prompted some concern on social media, for the most part fans are jubilant about the end of the “AO3 apocalypse,” as some have referred to the shutdown.
“Ao3 returned on a Sunday,” one fan wrote in a tweet that has 1.2 million views. “Just like Jesus.”

The people of Iraq are in urgent need of better health care and their situation is deteriorating by the day. The UN has today appealed for at least $325 million in emergency funds to meet the immediate health, nutrition, water and sanitation needs of the most vulnerable populations. Out of this amount, the World Health Organization urgently appeals for $185 million.
This request is part of the wider United Nations humanitarian appeal for $2.1 billion to provide assistance to the people of Iraq over the next six months. This appeal is being launched jointly by all the UN humanitarian agencies in New York and Geneva.
WHO is already working in Iraq to provide badly needed medical assistance. The health status of the Iraqi people has been seriously affected by more than two decades of war and economic sanctions. Child death rates today are more than twice as high as they were in 1990: one in eight children dies before the age of five, one in three children is malnourished and one in four begins life as an underweight baby.
"Overall, the health of people in Iraq is poor and likely to get worse," said Dr Gro Harlem Brundtland, Director General of the World Health Organization. "This appeal is not an optional extra. It is the only way of stabilising the situation, and indeed improving it."
The three biggest child killers in Iraq are acute respiratory infection, diarrhoeal diseases and measles. Almost half of the country's 24.5 million people are children whose future depends on a massive and rapid improvement in the country's health and infrastructure.
Conflict is already adding to the strains on the health of the population and on the infrastructure on which they depend. For example, damage to the electricity and water supply in the southern city of Basra is expected to lead to additional health problems, particularly for children and other vulnerable groups. People elsewhere may soon face similar or worse emergencies.
A substantial investment is needed to provide essential care to people who are either injured in the conflict or whose health suffers as a result of damage to the infrastructure. In the months to come, more will be needed to begin rebuilding the most critical and most badly effected parts of the public health system.
That means building up the capacities of hospitals and health centres; it means providing some $60 million of medicines, medical supplies and equipment; it means repairing and rehabilitating vital hospitals and health centres.
There must be substantial investment in the ability to detect and respond to outbreaks of disease, in the training and equipment of health workers and in the health information which is vital to prioritise health work.
WHO today has more than 300 staff working hard in Iraq to support the health system and to bring badly needed medical assistance to people across the country. During the current conflict, WHO has successfully sent teams to help with an outbreak of diarrhoeal disease in northern Iraq and to assess the health needs of people who have left their homes. WHO is ready to do much more work across the whole country in support of the health system.
In the weeks and months to come, Iraq's health system will almost inevitably come under unprecedented pressure. Health is a crucial part of the economic and social system.

13 killed, 31 injured in two accidents in Uttarakhand's Tehri and Rudraprayag
In the first accident, nine people were killed and 25 others injured after a passenger bus veered off the road and plunged into a 100-metre-deep gorge in Tehri.
Thirteen people were killed and 31 others injured in two separate road accidents in Uttarakhand’s Tehri and Rudraprayag districts between Monday night and Tuesday morning, police and officials said.
In the first accident, nine people were killed and 25 others injured after a passenger bus veered off the road and plunged into a 100-metre-deep gorge near Gular in Tehri district early on Tuesday morning.
According to officials, the accident occurred around 4:30 am near Gular market when the bus (registration number UK09PA-9779), en route from Haridwar to Chamoli, lost control and fell off the Gular bridge into a ravine below.
“Upon receiving the alert, a State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) team from the Byasi post rushed to the spot and launched rescue operations. Given the severity of the crash, additional teams from the Dhalwala post and the battalion headquarters were also dispatched to the spot,” SDRF Commandant Arpan Yaduvashi said.
Deep Dive
Yaduvashi said that SDRF personnel, braving difficult terrain and adverse conditions, carried out an intensive joint rescue operation alongside local police, administration officials, and residents.
“Rescuers extricated 26 injured passengers from the mangled vehicle and carried them up the steep slope to the roadhead on stretchers, from where they were shifted to nearby hospitals by ambulance. The bodies of the eight deceased were recovered from the wreckage and sent to hospital for post-mortem examination," Yaduvanshi said.
One person died later in the hospital
The official added that rescue teams conducted a thorough search of the surrounding area to ensure no passengers remained trapped before concluding the operation.
Another vehicle falls into a gorge
In the second accident, four people were killed and six others injured after a Bolero fell into a deep gorge on the Banswara-Mohankhal motor road in Rudraprayag district late on Monday night, police said.
The vehicle, bearing registration number UK13TA-1013, was travelling from the Pokhari area towards Ransi when the accident occurred. Police received information through Dial 112. The vehicle was reported to be carrying around 9-10 people.
Teams from Agastyamuni police, SDRF and District Disaster Response Force (DDRF), along with a 108 ambulance, were rushed to the spot. The rescue operation continued through the night as personnel brought the occupants out of the deep gorge.
Four people died in the accident, while six others were injured and taken to hospital. Two of the injured suffered minor injuries, while four were referred to a higher medical centre in Srinagar for further treatment.
More than 1,000 road accidents are reported in Uttarakhand every year, with the state’s treacherous, winding and narrow mountain roads often increasing the risk. The danger becomes more acute during the monsoon and winter seasons because of poor visibility and difficult road conditions. With the aim of reducing road accidents by 50% by 2030, the Uttarakhand cabinet approved the Road Safety Policy, 2025, in February 2025.

New Delhi, Nov 17: The government has hiked the windfall gains tax on exports of diesel and ATF and retained the levy at zero on petrol for the fortnight beginning November 16.
For ATF exports, the duty has been hiked to Rs 12.5/litre, from Rs 11/litre for the fortnight.
The rate of special additional excise duty (SAED) along with road and infrastructure cess on export of diesel will now be Rs 14/litre, up from Rs 11.5 a litre.
Duty on petrol exports has been retained at zero for the fortnight.
The Finance Ministry, in a late-night notification on November 16, said the duty changes will be effective immediately.
Amid escalating tensions in West Asia, the government imposed an export duty on diesel and ATF on March 27 and revised the rate every fortnight.
Beginning May 16, the levy was imposed on petrol exports.
The ministry also said that there is no change in the existing duty rates on petrol and diesel cleared for domestic consumption.
The windfall tax was levied to increase domestic availability of the fuel amid the war in West Asia.
It was also aimed at preventing exporters from taking undue advantage due to price differences as global crude oil prices had risen since the war began.

A proposal by the Trump administration to cap the amount of time foreign students and scholars can spend in the country has been struck down in court.
In a Monday ruling, Boston federal Judge F. Dennis Saylor IV wrote that the rule “is arbitrary, capricious, an abuse of discretion, and otherwise not in accordance with law.”
Saylor previously blocked the rule temporarily on the day before the policy was set to take effect. Monday’s ruling is a final decision on the case, though an appeal from the government on the initial ruling is still pending. Universities and research advocates worried that the four-year cap on visas could deter international students from pursuing graduate studies in the U.S., because such degrees often take longer than four years.

Visage Lines Personal Care Pvt Ltd, the parent entity of D2C grooming startup Bombay Shaving Company, has forayed into the wellness category with the launch of a new brand, called rE. Cofounded by Bombay Shaving Company chief marketing officer (CMO) Varun Gupta, the new brand sells a range of massage guns, scalp massagers, foam rollers and hot and cold packs. Its website went live on November 16. In addition, rE also noted that it is also building a separate sub-brand called Republic. Under this, it plans to set up a network of gyms and fitness-centric brands to tap into the recovery and health category. As per its website, products start from ₹349 for an eye mask and go all the way to ₹9,999 for a foot massager. “... A reset that takes ten minutes and is designed with doctors, not just around them, can become a habit. We think rE can help make daily recovery as normal as brushing your teeth,” said Bombay Shaving Company founder and CEO Shantanu Deshpande. In a statement, the startup also said that rE is pursuing partnerships with brands in areas such as fitness, sports and workplace wellness. “rE is pursuing partnerships across fitness, sport and workplace wellness, with a focus on bringing recovery into environments where people already train, compete and work. She went to college to become a social worker. Now she's joined the skilled trades
Sign up for alerts on breaking news and exclusive reporting from NPR
COLUMBUS, Ohio — A few miles south of The Ohio State University, Ashley Baukman is wrestling with a piece of steel tubing, using only a manual tool called a foot pedal and her sheer strength to bend it 90 degrees.
This class in conduit bending at The Electrical Trades Center of Central Ohio is part of an apprenticeship program Baukman began in the spring. She's here in class one day out of every two weeks. Other days, she's out on construction sites, working under the supervision of journeymen electricians.
For the 36-year-old college graduate and licensed social worker, it's a new chapter — one she hopes will be the foundation of a long-term career.
College didn't deliver
Being the first in her family to graduate from college had been a point of pride for Baukman.
"I was like, 'Oh, I'm going to do this. I'm going to do it the right way,'" she says. "But it didn't really work out that way, and that's okay. You live and you learn."
Now, as an apprentice, she's getting paid just over $25 an hour for time on the job and a stipend for days she's in class. Already, she's earning more than she was as a social worker and is set to nearly double her wage in just over three years. So far, she's finding the work engaging and rewarding.
"You can see a project to completion, and you can — 'Hey, I did that,'" she says. "It's been pretty fun."
A high point for apprenticeships
With AI throwing into question the future of work and the cost of college higher than ever, apprenticeships in the skilled trades are having a moment.
Once pushed primarily to the non-college bound, apprenticeships are increasingly being seen as a compelling alternative to higher education for anyone curious about the trades. The earn-as-you-learn model, which combines coursework with on-the-job training, requires no prerequisites or prior work experience. Acceptance is generally based on contractor need.
Right now demand for skilled tradespeople — especially electricians — is up.
The construction boom fueled by data centers has contributed to the rapid expansion of The Electrical Trades Center. Enrollment has grown from 500 apprentices in 2022 to more than 800 today. Once a night school, they now hold daytime classes to accommodate the growth.
Baukman may be the only licensed social worker among the apprentices, but as a college graduate, she has plenty of company. Trent Parker, the center's director and an electrician himself, says several dozen currently enrolled have four-year degrees, and roughly 300 applicants have at least some college on their resumes.
While Parker hasn't tracked the share of college graduates in the apprenticeship over the years, he's confident it's rising as sentiment toward the trades has shifted.
Parker recalls a recruiting visit he made to a technical high school 16 years ago. The school's vice principal told him they were grateful for the visit because they needed more opportunities for students who were "flunking out."
Parker was taken aback at the comment. He had just started as the apprenticeship's instruction coordinator and was realizing how deep the misconceptions run, how little this vice principal knew about the rigors of the work. That's now changing.
"You know, we're looking for high performers," Parker says. "The same people that are going to be successful in college are the same people that are going to be successful here."
He notes that the apprenticeship's curriculum is equivalent to college-level coursework. Conduit bending is based on trigonometry. Apprentices have to be able to manipulate decimals and fractions.
Parker was thrilled when in 2023, Ohio's governor signed into law a requirement that licensed school counselors visit a training center like this one to learn about apprenticeships and the careers they lead to, a major step in changing the "college or bust" mentality and recruiting more broadly into the field.
When his own two daughters were deciding about college, he encouraged them to consider following in his path.
"I asked them several times, 'Are you sure you don't want to be an electrician?'" he says. "Now I get to log into their Sallie Mae loan accounts and — you know — ugh. I agreed to pay what?"
Rethinking earlier choices
Gather together some of the college graduates at The Electrical Trades Center, and you hear similar themes. A common one: Careers they pursued after college just didn't pay enough.
After finishing her degree in social work, Baukman found jobs in local government agencies working with children and seniors but never earned enough to support her blended family. Her last job was as a prevention specialist in schools, but what she really wanted to do was to become a school social worker, a role that requires a master's degree. With five children at home, plus an estimated $80,000 in student loans, she couldn't figure out how to make it work.
"It just wasn't in the cards," she says. "So I was looking for a change."
Mike Hansen entered the apprenticeship after completing college, ten years in the Army, and some graduate school. He was originally on track to do a doctoral degree in sport and performance psychology, but had seen how others who had gone into academia had struggled.
"They were doing 40 hours of teaching and zero hours of research for $40,000 a year," he says. He left school after finishing his master's degree.
Now, at 39, he wishes he could go back and tell his 17-year-old self to consider a career in the trades from the start. The opportunity was there. His father was an airline mechanic and a member of the Teamsters union. His high school had a vocational school attached to it, but going there was highly stigmatized.
"I distinctly remember as part of our generation... it was massively looked down upon. You were considered a burnout," he says. "Guidance counselors, teachers, my parents, everyone was like, 'Go to college, get an engineering degree. You'll make six figures.'"
For Michael Hughes, the message was slightly different. "The expectation was to get a four-year degree in some field whatsoever, and you'll be fine," he says.
He wasn't sure what he wanted to do, so he majored in English.
"I had a pipe dream of, you know, writing for TV and movies," he says. After college, he did work for a time for the Geek Squad, mounting televisions and installing home theater systems, among other jobs.
Now, as an apprentice, he's been pulling wire, adding pipe, and replacing panels and fuses in a variety of settings including a police station, a paper mill, a sheet metal plant and an auto plant. He's appreciating the breadth of what he's learning and the chance to apply it immediately.
"It's almost like learning a foreign language by just going to that country and communicating, and then also taking classes and someone teaching you the proper conjugations of verbs," he says.
A future of six-figure earnings
Between new construction, commercial renovations and the data center buildout, electricians in Ohio are flush with work. With data center projects in particular, contractors are offering big incentives to get the jobs done quickly.
Parker has heard of projects paying $5 or $10 over the union-negotiated hourly wage. On other projects, all overtime is double time. There's even a rumor about triple time.
"There's some crazy money to be made out there," he says.
The apprentices are guaranteed a minimum hourly wage that starts at $23 an hour. There are built-in raises that come as they reach milestones for hours worked, topping out at $46 an hour. With overtime, many journeyworker electricians earn well over $100,000 a year, something the apprentices are looking forward to.
For now, these apprentices don't get to choose where they work. The program assigns them, based on contractor need. Harry Cekovich has been happy with his assignment at a solar field, where he's primarily running cables through rows of solar panels. There too, he's been picking up overtime while also collecting a $100 per diem. It's money he puts towards gas, although the site is less than an hour from his home.
Cekovich is the only one in the group who knows what it's like to earn six figures. For a time, the 34-year-old Ohio State graduate was making pretty good money as a massage therapist and a bartender.
"Granted, I was working 60, 70 hour weeks," he says. "Crazy, nonstop hours, so nothing too great, honestly."
None of those jobs came with benefits. Now, through the union contract, he has both retirement benefits and health insurance with no premiums.
"It's nice to be able to go to doctors and get checked up now," he says.
Mixed feelings about data centers and AI
With all the data center construction around Columbus, it's a given that the apprentices will work on a data center at some point. Some are more excited about it than others.
"If it's true about them making double or triple time… I want to work at data centers exclusively," jokes Cekovich.
Hansen is not so enthusiastic.
"There's enough concern and discussion going on right now about the harms that data centers cause," he says, citing their heavy energy and water use and the noise they generate. "Once I become a journeyman, and I'm allowed to pick my calls, I probably won't pick a job call for a data center, personally."
Ohio Gov.-elect Amy Acton has called for a "conditional moratorium" on new data center construction to ensure that developers cover their own utility costs, adhere to environmental standards and use union labor, among other things.
Whatever happens, Hansen expects there will be plenty of work at area hospitals, schools, commercial buildings and factories.
The apprentices are aware that the rapid buildout of data centers — especially hyperscale ones built to power AI — is a big reason the apprenticeship has been able to bring in so many recruits. At the moment, it accounts for about half the work in the school's jurisdiction.
"It kind of seems like it is, for better or worse, the way of the future," says Cekovich, adding that the proliferation of data centers influenced his decision to go into the electrical trades. "Are we contributing to the end of civilization with AI getting to be what it might become? Not totally sure."
Come what may, Hansen believes he and his classmates will be okay.
"I would like to see Chat GPT wire a three-way switch," he says. "We're still going to need electricians."

Madurai City Police have made full recovery of the over 11 kg of gold and diamond jewellery stolen from Tanishq showroom in the city following the arrest of prime accused of the gold heist, S. Nishanth (23), on Monday (November 16, 2026).
Nishanth who has been on the run since the theft at the newly-inaugurated showroom on Bypass Road, was arrested by a police team in Dharmapuri district on Monday.
He was brought to Madurai the same night and was grilled by senior police officers, including the Deputy Commissioner of Police (South), A.G. Inigo Thivyan. Based on his confession, the police took him to a secluded place at Madakulam and recovered another cache of the booty which was left buried.
The police had already recovered over 5 kg of the stolen ornaments after the arrest of Nishanth’s father, Suresh as well as his friend and social media influencer, Meenakshi. “We have recovered till the last gram of the gold intact,” an officer from Madurai City Police told The Hindu.
Later, Nishanth was produced before a judicial magistrate who ordered his remand in judicial custody till December 1. The accused was lodged in Madurai central prison.
Bus crew’s help in nabbing Nishanth
Interrogation revealed that the youth was arrested by the police when the crew of an omnibus got suspicious over his movement with him wearing a face mask. He had also sought mobile phone from a crew member to make a call.
“It was then he got suspicious over Nishanth and alerted his driver. Even as the bus was moving, the driver had informed about this suspect in the bus to one of his friends in the police,” the officer said.
Later, the police asked the driver to keep the bus running slowly up to a particular spot to facilitate the team to reach the bus. The driver stopped the bus after locking the passenger door and got down. By then, Nishanth who got suspicious, jumped out of the bus through the driver’s door.
When questioned by the driver, Nishanth had told him that his friend was coming to pick him up. However, the police team arrived at the spot by then. As Nishanth took to heels, the police chased him and nabbed him.
Family’s debt
Nishanth reportedly confessed to the police that he turned to burglary as his family was in huge debt and also his friend Meenakshi was struggling to find resources for constructing a house. Since, he had been passing through the Bypass Road frequently, he noticed the construction of the building of Tanishq showroom and planned the heist, the police said.
After the burglary, he was going around Madurai city for the first two days. As his name surfaced as a suspect and was doing rounds on social media, he fled to Kodaikanal, Coimbatore, Salem and then Hosur. He was caught on his way back to Madurai in the omni bus.

Six months after an Ebola outbreak was declared in Congo, the disease remains out of control and efforts to contain it are faltering.
More than 11,000 cases have been recorded, and nearly half of those infected have died, according to Government data. It is the deadliest of Congo's 17 outbreaks and is on track to surpass the death toll from the West African outbreak that killed 11,000 people between 2014 and 2016.
Basic containment measures, including contact tracing and isolation, remain inadequate, raising doubts about authorities' ability to halt the outbreak. Experts say there is little chance of bringing it under control within the next year.
By the time the outbreak was announced in mid-May, 43 deaths had already been recorded, suggesting the virus had circulated undetected for an extended period. It has since spread to eight of the country's 26 provinces, moving at a pace aid groups have likened to wildfire.
New hotspots continue to emerge, stretching an already strained health care system.
Questions over funding and management
Community transmission remains high. According to the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention, 80% of new cases are being detected outside health surveillance, meaning most infections have not been tracked by authorities.
One-third of deaths occur at home or elsewhere in the community, where burials and other procedures are often conducted without specialist supervision, increasing the risk of transmission.
Health workers have repeatedly gone on strike over pay that is months overdue, sometimes leaving patients with confirmed infections without treatment.
Aid groups have also questioned how the response is being managed. Last month, the Africa CDC raised concerns about more than $700 million in Ebola aid that remains unaccounted for.
“A troubling disconnect between the considerable resources mobilised for the response and what is actually reaching patients, frontline workers, and communities continues,” said the humanitarian organisation Doctors Without Borders, known by its French acronym MSF.
Children face high death rates
Children are particularly vulnerable to Ebola, especially those with preexisting conditions such as malnutrition, experts say.
Most children affected by the disease have not received specialised care, contributing to high death rates.
According to UNICEF, children accounted for 35% of deaths recorded through November 4. Children under 5 accounted for 21% of all deaths, and nearly 72% of infected children in that age group have died.
Conflict and attacks hamper response
Health workers face difficult conditions as Ebola prevention and containment measures clash with social and cultural practices.
Since the outbreak began, health workers have been attacked, some fatally, adding to the dangers of working in an already volatile region. Health facilities have also come under attack.
The outbreak has been concentrated in eastern Congo, particularly Ituri and North Kivu, where communities face both the epidemic and armed conflict.
Fighting between Government forces and hundreds of rebel groups, including the Rwanda-backed M23, had already helped create one of the world's most severe humanitarian crises. The Allied Democratic Forces, an Islamic State-affiliated rebel group, also attacks civilians.
The virus's rapid spread has raised fears of wider transmission across Africa. Nigeria, Kenya and Uganda have confirmed cases, making this the most geographically widespread Ebola outbreak on record.

Monica was not prepared for a caesarean section. She had done everything right and had been assured of a vaginal delivery. Then two weeks before the expected date of delivery, she had to be rushed to the emergency for a caesarean. Monica felt that she had completely lost control of the situation. She found herself alone in an intensive care ward away from her baby, who was in the neonatal ICU and described her birth experience as being extremely traumatic. She is now unable to bond with her baby and keeps questioning herself. Am I such a terrible mother? Will I be like this lifelong?
Priya became pregnant after multiple IVF procedures but did not disclose the pregnancy to anyone till the third trimester, as she didn’t want to jinx it. After a healthy baby girl was born, Priya continued to be anxious and could not trust anyone else to take care of the baby. She would be hypervigilant, and even the smallest change in the infant’s spit-up or breathing would make her panic.

FIFA has joined forces with the United Nations (UN) and the World Health Organization (WHO) in supporting the #BeActive campaign launched on the UN International Day of Sport for Development and Peace to encourage people to be #HealthyAtHome as the world comes together in the fight against COVID-19, today and every day.
WHO recommends all healthy adults do at least 30 minutes a day of physical activity and children at least 60 minutes per day. As part of this, #BeActive and remain #HealthyAtHome include the following suggestions along with any other form of recreation to stay healthy at home:
- Taking some online exercise classes,
- Dancing,
- Playing active video games,
- Jumping rope, and
- Practising muscle strength and balance training.
“We are delighted that football is strongly supporting the International Day of Sport for Development and Peace by asking everyone to #BeActive and to remain healthy at home during this difficult time,” said António Guterres Secretary-General of the United Nations. “FIFA has asked the football community, from member associations and clubs, to players and fans, to show their support, to put their rivalries aside and to show a new solidarity so we can overcome the coronavirus. This is an important lesson not only for today, but for every day.”
“More than ever, especially now, one thing must be clear to everyone, health comes first,” said FIFA President Gianni Infantino. “FIFA is delighted to support both the United Nations and the World Health Organization in amplifying the #BeActive campaign today, and we are encouraged that the football community is also playing an active role in ensuring the message understood globally. For the first time ever, we are all on the same team and together, with team spirit and positive energy, we will win.”
“WHO is proud to collaborate as part of the UN family with FIFA and football lovers worldwide to promote the importance of being active for both physical and mental health,” said Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, Director-General of the World Health Organization. “The #BeActive campaign supports WHO’s drive to help people be healthy at home.”
The campaign kicks off with Real Madrid CF, FC Barcelona, Liverpool FC and Manchester United FC asking football fans to set aside their rivalries and to come together to #BeActive in order to defeat the coronavirus. Other clubs, including Club América, CD Guadalajara, Beijing Guoan FC, Shanghai Shenhua FC, Mohun Bagan AC, East Bengal FC, Melbourne City FC, Sydney FC, Auckland City FC, Team Wellington FC, CA River Plate, Olympique de Marseille, TP Mazembe, CR Flamengo and SE Palmeiras will also join the initiative in the coming days.
As part of the campaign, world-famous players share the following message: “At this time, even rivals need to stick together. We have to keep our distance, but we do not lose our focus. We can show solidarity by being active, and active means following the guidelines from the WHO.”
The video campaign will be published on various FIFA digital channels, with regular subsequent updates from clubs and players across the world during subsequent days. #BeActive is also being supported with graphics toolkits for the 211 FIFA member associations and various media agencies to facilitate additional localisation and to further amplify the message.
WHO, the UN’s specialized health agency, and FIFA, football’s world governing body, collaborate closely to promote healthy lifestyles through football globally and launched the “ Pass the message to kick out coronavirus” campaign last month to share advice effective measures to protect people from COVID-19.
The video campaign can also be downloaded here for editorial purposes.

Meta has tightened Instagram’s recommendation filters in India to show less sexually suggestive and violent content. The changes apply to posts from accounts users don’t follow that Instagram recommends across Explore, Reels, and Feed. In a blog post, Meta said it strengthened Instagram’s default safeguards in India over the past year based on user feedback. Separately, the company has upgraded its detection systems globally with AI models that check posts against Instagram’s recommendation guidelines before surfacing them, without relying on users to report or hide them. Meta said users in India now report recommended content about half as often as they did a year ago. The company did not disclose the absolute number of reports or how much content it had filtered out. Instagram users can further limit sensitive content in Search, Reels, Explore, Feed recommendations, and suggested accounts through Sensitive Content Control. They can also use Political Content Control to see less political content from accounts they don’t follow, or select ‘Not Interested’ from a post or reel’s menu to shape future recommendations. Meta Faces Regulatory Scrutiny The recommendation update comes amid regulatory scrutiny of Meta over the alleged circulation and promotion of child sexual abuse material (CSAM) on Instagram. A BBC investigation alleged that paid Instagram ads directed users to Telegram channels offering CSAM. The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) summoned Meta executives following the allegations, and the National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR) opened an inquiry. In September, Meta agreed to report child safety cases directly to Indian authorities through the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal, operated by the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C). Later, the company said it had taken action against 5.3 Mn pieces of child sexual exploitation content across Facebook and Instagram in India in the first half of 2026. Meta said it identified and acted on more than 98% of that content before users reported it. Meanwhile, the Centre is also exploring withdrawing safe harbour protection under Section 79 of the IT Act for social media platforms such as Facebook, Instagram, YouTube, and X. The protection limits platforms’ liability for user-generated content.

British government ministers were told not to engage formally with Vantara, the controversial mega-zoo run by the Indian billionaire Anant Ambani, after lobbying efforts by the private animal sanctuary in the run-up to a UK-chaired meeting on the trade in endangered species, according to documents.
This week, the UK heads a 32-country committee meeting in Geneva of Cites, the United Nations body that regulates trade in endangered species. The meeting will examine how India has responded to compliance concerns about imports of endangered animals.
Documents obtained by the Guardian and the news outlet Mongabay under the UK’s Freedom of Information Act reveal Vantara’s efforts to lobby British officials and ministers before the meeting.
Ambani, 31, is the heir to the oil and gas fortune of one of India’s richest men, Mukesh Ambani. He set up a 1,400-hectare (3,500-acre) private zoo near his family’s oil-refining facilities in Gujarat, where more than 150,000 animals have reportedly been amassed since 2022. Vantara boasts high welfare standards for animals in its care, including facilities such as an elephant hydrotherapy pool, where more than 260 elephants can also receive oil therapies and Ayurvedic massage.
But conservation groups have repeatedly questioned how such a vast number of species, many of which are endangered, were gathered so quickly. Last year, India’s supreme court cleared the zoo’s operators of any wrongdoing.
A subsequent Cites fact-finding mission looking into the zoo raised concerns about India’s compliance with international rules on animal imports in 2025. It recommended temporary restrictions on India, although the recommendation was later withdrawn.
Its November 2025 report said: “There is a need for caution to ensure that imports of large numbers of animals by these facilities are not inadvertently creating a demand for illegally sourced animals.”
In May, officials from the UK’s Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs (Defra) met a representative from Vantara and the US lobbyist firm Checkmate Government Relations, founded by Ches McDowell, a hunting friend of Donald Trump Jr.
Before the meeting, internal briefing documents said Checkmate was “seeking to persuade the UK to take a more sympathetic view of India’s handling of imports to Vantara and of Checkmate’s argument that responsibility for verifying legality sits primarily with exporting or re-exporting parties rather than with India as importer”.
During the meeting, the Vantara representative invited UK officials to visit the zoo – an invitation that was subsequently declined to ensure the impartiality of the UK’s Cites chair role.
After the meeting, a representative from another lobbying firm, Atlas Strategy, working on behalf of Vantara, approached the then secretary of state, Emma Reynolds, and then nature minister, Mary Creagh, also raising the prospect of a visit to the zoo.
When a department official asked for advice, a note was issued recommending that ministers did not engage formally with Vantara.
The government documents also reveal concerns about an application by Vantara to import falcons and falcon hybrids, after an unnamed organisation made a £50,000 “donation” to a breeder in the UK, whose identity was also not disclosed. British Cites officials classified the transaction as commercial, according to the documents. The falcons were not exported to India.
A spokesperson for Vantara said it had not imported falcons from the UK, nor had the zoo hired or paid a lobbying firm. It is understood that Checkmate and Altas Strategy were working pro bono for Vantara and not required to register with the Office of the Registrar of Consultant Lobbyists.
After recent scrutiny, Vantara has sought to “reset” its activities by voluntarily suspending animal imports for a year and hiring John Scanlon, a former Cites chief, to oversee its operations. In an interview with the Sunday Times this year, Ambani said he only brought animals to Vantara legally to ensure their welfare, mentioning a group of hippos he had saved from a hunting lodge in South Africa and jackass penguins saved from a shopping centre in Qatar.
“I think since I was a baby I have been taking care of animals. It’s always been a passion,” he said.
Vantara was used to host Ambani’s lavish pre-wedding celebrations in 2024, which were attended by celebrity guests and politicians. In September, Newcastle University awarded the oil heir a professorship of practice for “his work in conservation, biodiversity protection, animal welfare and environmental stewardship”, sparking a backlash from conservationists.
A Defra spokesperson said: “The UK has strict rules in place to protect endangered species and ensuring international wildlife trade is legal and sustainable, with every application assessed individually against internationally agreed and domestic requirements.”
